messages:
maria: Heads-up — after merge 4120 rolled to eu-central (A10 / L4) around 07:22 UTC we see a large p99 spike for long-sequence requests. Dashboard snapshot: p50 26ms -> 28ms, p95 120ms -> 145ms, p99 360ms -> 830ms. Flamegraph: https://perf.corp/flame/1948123456

Profile snippet:
```
kernel_selector: selected 'l4-quant-2' for seq_len=1024, batch=4
latency breakdown: kernel_invoke 62ms, memcpy_h2d 18ms, memcpy_d2h 20ms
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.12 -> 0.45
```
Anyone else seeing a region-specific regression?

devin: @maria saw CI perf-check fail on merge 4120 too. PR touched the kernel-selector heuristics (we now prefer l4-quant-2 for batch_size>2). My guess: selector picks a suboptimal kernel for our small-batch long-seq traffic. Adding verbose selector logs now. :eyes:

ci-bot: perf-check FAILED for merge 4120
- delta p99: +130%
- run: https://ci.corp/runs/4120/perf
- regression window: HEAD~5..HEAD

rahul: Interesting — us-west dedicated A10 pools didn't show the same regression. Could be different request mix or noisy neighbors in eu-central (we had an infra alert ~07:18 UTC).

sre-jen: We did have a noisy VM migration in eu-central at 07:18 UTC that increased NIC queue depth on some racks. That could amplify p99, but @maria you said isolated nodes also repro?

maria: Correct — I repro'd on an isolated A10 instance with no co-tenants. Microbench reproduces the p99 increase. Quick git diff shows selector tweak + a batching heuristic change in commit c4a7 that look suspicious. I'm starting a bisect between c3f..c4a7.

devin: Try forcing the kernel back to the legacy path to confirm. You can set env var KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy or export REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=l4-quant-1 and rerun the microbench. If p99 drops, selector change is likely culprit.

maria: Ran that. Forcing legacy kernel (l4-quant-1) drops p99 to ~380ms (close to pre-merge). Strong indicator the selector change is the root cause. Bisecting now.

rahul: One more datapoint: your profile shows kv_cache_miss_rate jumped — could selector choice affect prefetch logic and therefore cache behavior? If l4-quant-2 disables a prefetch path, miss rate spike would explain higher latency.

maria: Good catch. I added counters and here's an immediate snapshot from the microbench:
```
kv_cache_hits=880
kv_cache_misses=320
prefetch_calls=0
```
prefetch_calls=0 looks wrong for this workload.

devin: The PR added an optimization to skip prefetch for kernels claiming fused attention. Seems we accidentally returned fused=true for l4-quant-2 in some codepaths. That would disable prefetch.

sre-jen: Proposed immediate actions:
1) Hold the rollout of 4120 in eu-central (put canary/rollout on hold).
2) Open a revert for the selector tweak in canary and run targeted perf tests on A10/L4.
3) Add a CI perf gate that checks p99 on small-batch long-seq workload for A10 L4. I'll set the rollout hold now.

maria: I'm opening a targeted revert PR with microbench that reproduces the failure and a failing test asserting kv_cache_miss_rate < 0.2 for our sample trace. Also logging the bisect results in the PR.

devin: Ping me on the PR — I'll help craft the reproducer and verify the prefetch fix. Also let's add a unit test for kernel selection semantics to prevent future accidental fused=true regressions.

maria: Created PR: https://git.corp/pr/4289 — "revert: kernel-selector tweak from 4120 + prefetch guard". Assigned to devin, requested infra review. I'll post perf results here once CI finishes.

ci-bot: Scheduled perf-run for PR 4289. ETA ~15m.

sre-jen: Rollout held in eu-central, alerting support, and adding note to #release-holds. Will follow up after CI run. :thumbsup:
